summary: Spirit Airlines has celebrated reaching 69 planes by offering round‑trip flights for £69, complete with tongue‑in‑cheek promotional copy that highlights the number 69 as a favorite. The carrier, known for its “Home of the Bare Fare” branding, uses quirky, provocative marketing to distinguish itself from traditional airlines. Some customers have taken to social media questioning whether the campaign is too edgy.
reference:
To celebrate their newest aircraft, Spirit is offering $69 roundtrip fares .
Announced the promotion with several emails full of sexual innuendo .
Some customers have complained that the campaign is in poor taste .

summary: Wales topped Group B after a 3‑0 win over Israel, with Aaron Ramsey’s goal celebrating his late grandmother. Ramsey believes the Welsh side can shock world‑ranking Belgium in their June 12 home match, citing their confidence and recent solid performances. Meanwhile, Belgium thrashed Cyprus 5‑0, with Marouane Fellaini and Eden Hazard scoring, leaving Wales poised to secure one of the two automatic qualifying spots if they continue winning.
reference:
Aaron Ramsey insists Wales can spring a surprise against Belgium .
Wales earned 3-0 Group B victory against Israel on Saturday night .
Chris Coleman's face Red Devils in Euro 2016 qualifier on June 12 .
Ramsey gave hosts the lead before Gareth Bale bagged a brace .

summary:
Former Treasurer Joe Hockey sued Fairfax Media for defamation after a headline “Treasurer for Sale” in major newspapers caused his family distress.  
He testified in Federal Court that the story ruined his reputation and even led his elderly father to question him, describing how he was devastated when he saw the front pages.  
Hockey argued the articles falsely implicated him in a fundraising forum, while Fairfax’s lawyers defended the coverage as accurate reporting.
reference:
Joe Hockey has testified as part of defamation suit against Fairfax media .
He appeared at the Federal Court on Monday and claimed that the article caused his family great distress, even making his elderly father cry .
The court action centres on stories run by Fairfax Media under the headline 'Treasurer for sale'
Mr Hockey claims that there was a  'clear allegation of corruption' within the North Sydney Forum, a political fundraising party in his electorate .

summary: Off‑duty officer Mark Hudson was shot dead in his Darby Township home, and his girlfriend Tyaina Finch was charged with murder and related offenses. Finch claimed the shooting was accidental after taking a gun from her dog, but police say she intended to kill him. Their relationship had been marked by repeated domestic disputes, including a knife threat last summer.
reference:
The girlfriend of an off-duty Pennsylvania police officer who was shot and killed over the weekend is in custody .
Tyaina Finch is charged with the murder of her boyfriend .
Police Officer Mark Hudson, 26 was shot .
The couple were said to have a 'tumultuous' relationship .

summary: Climate change is predicted to make meats tougher, seafood less tasty, and dairy products lower in protein, threatening the quality of staples like steaks, shrimp, milk and cheese. Ocean acidification could make shrimp 2.6 times more likely to taste bad, while heatwaves may cut grain and milk yields by up to 25 %. The University of Melbourne report warns that rising temperatures could also alter the flavor and availability of everyday foods such as avocados, bread, and even beer.
reference:
Report by University of Melbourne warns that many foods are under threat .
It says that heatwaves will cause livestock like cattle to suffer heat stress .
Beef and pork likely to become tougher while chicken will become stringer .
Onions and beetroot crops are likely to produce smaller sized vegetables .
Carrots will lose  their distinctive flavour and take on an unpleasant texture .
Milk yields can decrease by 10-25 per cent during heat waves, report warns .
Protein levels in milk may also fall meaning cheese will decline in quality .

summary: Australia’s latest self‑assessed “attractivity” study ranks Sydney as the most attractive city for singles, followed by Melbourne and Queensland’s Gold Coast. The top ten cities include Brisbane, Perth, Sunshine Coast, Newcastle, Coffs Harbour, Adelaide, and Canberra, with key suburbs highlighted in each city. Despite lower rankings, Darwin’s residents cite a rugged, down‑to‑earth appeal rather than conventional attractiveness.
reference:
Dating website Elite Singles surveyed 28,000 single Australians .
Participants aged 30-55 were asked to rate their level of attractiveness .
Sydneysiders claim they are the sexiest, with Melbourne and Gold Coast ranking in at second and third .
Darwin and Hobart prove more modest, sinking well below the top ten .

summary: Former kindergarten teacher Elliot Gornall was arrested on 25 felony charges for secretly filming dozens of students with a hidden camera in 2014. Authorities found the footage on his personal computer, and he had already resigned after a prior drug‑related arrest. Parents and the school district expressed shock, anger, and betrayal, and prosecutors warned he could face up to 184 years in prison if convicted.
reference:
Elliot Gornall, 32, was former teacher at RF McMullen Elementary School where he resigned from teaching last year following felony drug charges .
He is accused of using camera hidden inside plastic hook on wall of his classroom's bathroom to film students .
Investigators found dozens of videos featuring students on his computer .
Children's underwear were also discovered while searching his home in relation to previous drug charges in November .
No indication that any students were physically abused or touched inappropriately; Gornall faces 25 felony charges .

summary: The Bardo Museum attack in Tunis underscores a surge of Islamist terrorism across North and sub‑Saharan Africa, where groups like AQIM, ISIS affiliates, and Boko Haram have carried out high‑profile attacks. These incidents, which include massacres in Algeria, Libya, Mali, and Kenya, have claimed many foreign and local lives, prompting international concern. Tunisia, home to thousands of its citizens fighting abroad, is tightening security and considering anti‑terror legislation in response.
reference:
Islamist extremism poses a growing threat in parts of North and sub-Saharan Africa .
Extremist groups operating in Africa include ISIS, al Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb, Al Shabaab and Boko Haram .

summary: Eltham Palace, once a childhood home of Henry VIII, is reopening in April after a £1.7 million renovation that will unveil five new Art‑Deco rooms, a wartime bunker, and the lavish Courtauld family’s travel‑mapped interiors. The restoration, part of a £52 million conservation programme, also includes replanted gardens and displays of early artifacts such as a vacuum cleaner. Visitors will experience the palace’s historic great hall, luxurious bathrooms, and a new visitor centre with café, all while stepping back to the swinging 1930s.
reference:
The Eltham Palace in Greenwich has undergone a £1.7 million renovation .
The property was the childhood home of Henry VIII and has entertained many royals, politicians, and socialites .
Visitors will be able to view the restored Art Deco property, which was transformed in the 1930s, this April .

summary:
Richard Kilty, a former homeless teenager from Stockton-on-Tees, has risen from a troubled estate to become one of Britain’s fastest sprinters, winning gold in the 60 m at the European Indoor Championships.  
His background of violence, substance abuse and early life struggles fuels his determination to escape poverty and inspire others.  
Kilty also criticises doping in athletics, insisting he is clean while lamenting the prevalence of drug cheats.
reference:
Richard Kilty won  60m gold at the European Indoor Championships .
The sprinter grew up on a deprived estate in Stockton-on-Tees .
One of Kilty's friends drowned and another was sent to prison for burglary .
He had just £17 in his bank account when he won his first indoor gold .
Kilty briefly retired from athletics after failing to make the 2012 Olympics .
He is now targeting the World Championships with coach Linford Christie .

summary:
Christopher Kling was detained after a family friend showed police a video of him blowing marijuana fumes into his infant’s mouth.  
The incident occurred at his estranged wife’s home in Beaverton, Oregon, just before midnight.  
Kling faces three felony charges of applying a controlled substance to a minor.
reference:
Christopher Kling accused of blowing marijuana smoke into baby's mouth .
22-year-old arrested after police responded to reports of a disturbance .
A family friend said to have passed video of Kling and the infant to officers .
Charged with 3 counts of application of a controlled substance to a minor .

summary: David Cameron announced that the May 2020 general election would be his last, sparking debate over his decision to pre‑announce a departure. MPs and the media speculated on successors—Theresa May, Boris Johnson and George Osborne—while polling showed most voters considered his move honest, though a minority feared he would become a lame duck. The announcement has split opinion, with some praising his clarity and others warning it could undermine his authority before the election.
reference:
David Cameron said earlier this week that he would not bid for a third term .
Cameron said two terms were 'wonderful' but three 'might just be too many'
Named Boris Johnson, Theresa May and George Osborne as successors .
Has now insisted he was just giving ‘straight answer to a straight question’
PM also said he believed most people would think it was a ‘sensible’ thing .
Mr Cameron said yesterday Thomas the Tank Engine was the television character he most identified with. In an interview with Netmums.com, Mr Cameron said: ‘He’s a British icon, he’s blue, he’s loyal and reliable – and he always saves the day.’ Lib Dems leader Nick Clegg opted for Paddington Bear, while Labour’s Ed Miliband sees himself as Captain Barnacles.

summary: Gary Allen reflects on his growth from a disappointed first season at Liverpool to becoming a key player for club and Wales, noting the highs and lows of his career. He looks forward to a tough Euro qualifier against Israel, confident that his experience will help Wales maintain their unbeaten streak. At 25, Allen sees himself entering his peak, motivated by Wales' recent form and the historic gap since their near miss at Euro 2004.
reference:
Wales travel to Israel for a Euro 2016 qualifier that could define campaign .
Joe Allen does not grab headlines but plays an effective role for Wales .
Midfielder admitted he went though difficult spell when he joined Liverpool .
Allen says he has improved as a player after the bad experience .

summary: Saudi blogger Raif Badawi has spoken for the first time from prison, saying the first 50 of his 1,000 lashes were “miraculous.” He was sentenced in 2012 to lashes, ten years in jail and a 1 million‑riyal fine for insulting Islam. A book about his ordeal will be published in Germany, though officials warn it could endanger his life.
reference:
Raif Badawi has spoken for first time since being jailed for 'insulting Islam'
He recalled how cheering crowds chanted around him during first flogging .
Remarks will feature in book called '1,000 Lashes: Why I Say What I Think'
His sentence, including weekly beatings, sparked an international outcry .

summary:
A 13‑year‑old boy has pleaded guilty to stabbing builder Christopher John Barry to death during a row outside an Edmonton block of flats.  
The case, investigated by DCI Neale Baldock, shows no prior link between the victim and the youths, and the judge will sentence the teenager on April 10, with a minimum of 12 years in prison.  
Residents described the landing as covered in blood and noted longstanding problems with parties and intruders in the building.
reference:
Boy, 13, admits stabbing a builder outside a block of flats in north London .
Teenager pleaded guilty to murdering Christopher John Barry, who was 53 .
The 13-year-old will face a minimum of 12 years in jail after sentencing .
Mr Barry was said to have been involved in a row with a group of youths .
Two boys followed him into the building before he was stabbed, police said .

summary: Harry Roberts, 78, was released on licence after serving 48 years for killing three unarmed police officers in 1966. He now lives in a state‑funded bungalow, checks in twice a day, and leads a routine of shopping and gym visits. Authorities consider him low risk but plan to move him to different accommodation to avoid community recognition.
reference:
Harry Roberts was released from prison on licence in November last year .
He served 48 years behind bars for shooting three unarmed police officers .
Killer has to check in with authorities twice daily but is free to come and go .
The 78-year-old has been seen on bus to supermarket and buying bacon .
One neighbour described him as looking like 'the cat who got the cream'
His bail hostel, along with state pension, costing taxpayers £31,000 a year .

summary: An undercover reporter claimed a Lib Dem fundraiser instructed him on how to structure donations to stay below the £7,500 disclosure limit, using family members and back‑dating cheques. Treasury minister Danny Alexander was recorded urging further giving, but party leader Nick Clegg denied wrongdoing, calling his remarks merely polite thanks. The incident has spotlighted the Liberal Democrats’ fundraising practices and raised scrutiny over political donations.
reference:
Undercover reporter was allegedly told to split donation among family .
Move would allow him to keep his identity hidden, breaching election code .
Met with Danny Alexander who urged him to donate more, it is claimed .
Was allegedly promised high-level meetings with other senior Lib Dems .

summary: A mother of seven and her daughter were denied NHS surgery for lipodystrophy, so they received a free face and neck lift with Botox from U.S. doctors. The operation restored their appearance and significantly boosted their self‑esteem. Both now feel empowered, confident, and proud of their renewed sense of dignity.
reference:
Tracey Gibson and her daughter Zara Hartshorn both suffer Lipodystrophy .
The rare condition makes fat dissolve beneath tissue and wrinkles skin .
Zara, now 18, was offered free treatment in the U.S. when she was 16 .
Her mother, 45, was rejected by the NHS when she asked for a facelift .
American doctors have since treated her to the same deal as her daughter .
Face and neck lift as well as multiple Botox treatments were worth £50,000 .

summary: China has intensified its crackdown on Uighurs, prosecuting many for wearing beards, veils, or burqas and banning those with facial hair from public transport, while also offering rewards to informants. These actions have inflamed tensions in Xinjiang, resulting in violence that killed at least 200 people and heightened fears of separatism. The crackdown is part of a broader campaign to dilute Uighur cultural and religious identity amid accusations of suppressing minority freedoms.
reference:
38-year-old Uighur received several warnings before attending, official said .
His wife was also given a two-year sentence for hiding her face with a veil .

summary:
England missed the European title but delivered an exciting, high‑scoring performance.  
Ben Youngs and George Ford highlighted England’s potential, while gaps in back‑row pace were exposed.  
Strong displays from Wales and Ireland show a competitive tournament, with England looking to build on this experience for the World Cup.
reference:
England cut loose in thrilling fashion against France on Saturday .
Players know now that there is another level they can perform to .
Coach Stuart Lancaster can move forward with real confidence .

summary: Germanwings co‑pilot Andreas Lubitz, who deliberately crashed a jet in 2015 killing all 150 aboard, is seen in old footage flying a glider as a teenager, highlighting a long‑hidden battle with depression. Investigators uncovered medical records, pills and a “mountain of medication” in his home, prompting demands that doctors disclose health issues for safety‑critical roles. The case has spurred calls to relax doctor‑patient confidentiality for pilots to prevent future tragedies.
reference:
Andreas Lubitz, 27, captured on an in-flight camera taking off  in a glider .
Video believed to have been taken in Germany when he was in late teens .
Jokes with his companion: 'We're going until we have no more fuel, okay?'
Later trained as airline pilot in 2007 before taking six-month medical break .

summary: Reverend Phyllis Sortor, a 71‑year‑old missionary, was abducted on February 23 from Hope Academy in Kogi state and released Friday, with police and security forces securing her return. Bishop David Kendall confirmed her safe release into the care of authorities and Free Methodist Church leaders. Abductions in Nigeria are often ransom‑driven, and the lack of a claim by Boko Haram suggests the kidnapping was not Islamist‑motivated.
reference:
Masked gunman raided a Christian school and fired sporadically to scare people away before taking Phyllis Sortor hostage on February 23 .
Free Methodist Church USA announced she was released on Friday .
Gunmen previously demanded $300,000 for the reverend's release .
Sorter has been working as a missionary for the past ten years .

summary: Fantastic Pit in Ellison's Cave, Georgia, plunges 586 ft underground—twice the height of the Statue of Liberty—and is part of a 12‑mile system that is notoriously pitch‑black and technically demanding. Despite being a favorite of thrill‑seekers, the cave has claimed several lives, mainly from hypothermia and rope entanglements in its vertical sections. Experienced cavers are advised to use proper training, gear, and single‑rope techniques before attempting the pit.
reference:
Fantastic Pit in Ellison's Cave, Georgia, USA, is 586ft deep - twice the height of the Statue of Liberty .
Climbers completed the descent and and produced a stunning set of photograph of the cave system .
One of the group, Amy Hinkle, insists if proper training is done, 'caving is a relatively safe sport'

summary: A stalled jet stream kept Alaska warm and dry, so Anchorage had only a third of its usual snow but still staged the Iditarod ceremonial start by hauling in snow and hosting fans and mushers. The event highlighted popular mushers, but was marred when a sled dog was killed by a car on Seward Highway. This year’s race will feature 78 mushers, a $70,000 purse, and a new route that omits the dangerous Alaska Range.
reference:
Race started on Saturday with a ceremonial run through Anchorage despite the lack of snow .
Organizers have been forced to move the competitive start of the race further north to Fairbanks, where it will start on Monday .
City crews overnight delivered up to 350 dump truck loads of snow and spread it out over city blocks so the show could go on Saturday .
Fans lined the streets and cheered on the mushers and their Iditariders, who are people who have won auctions to be in the sled .

summary: David Beckham attended a London performance of *Lord of the Dance* with his family. After the show he met star Michael Flatley, who was grieving his father’s recent death, and exchanged supportive messages. Meanwhile, Victoria Beckham highlighted her new eyewear line in Hong Kong.
reference:
Whole family checked out Michael Flatley's farewell Lord Of The Dance show on Saturday .
Flatley's beloved father died just one day before and David praised the dancer for going ahead with Saturday's performance .
Michael shared a picture of himself and David and thanked the footballer for his support .
He has vowed to continue the farewell tour but will take time out to attend his father's wake in Chicago this week .

summary: A Hove call‑centre reportedly made 4–6 million unsolicited calls a day to more than 90 million UK numbers, targeting vulnerable and elderly people with debt‑consolidation and PPI‑compensation offers. The ICO raided the firm and is investigating whether it illegally sold customer data to other companies. Authorities say the operation was unprecedented in scale and may lead to criminal prosecution if data was passed on without authorisation.
reference:
Call centre left 'millions upon millions' of anonymous phone messages .
It appeared to have 'cornered' sizeable proportion of cold-call market .
Office said to have bombarded people with offers to consolidate debts .
Also said it could help people pursue compensation claim for mis-sold PPI .

summary:
Dr Hirono, a UK-based international relations expert, was denied indefinite leave to remain after spending over 180 days abroad, forcing her and her family to relocate to Kyoto.  
The decision, criticized as vindictive by colleagues and MPs, was upheld by the Home Office despite her research funding and policy contributions.  
Hirono argues the ruling exposes a broader problem for the UK’s recruitment of foreign professionals.
reference:
Dr Miwa Hirono has been a lecturer at University of Nottingham for 7 years .
She is originally from Japan and her research is famous around the world .
In 2010 she spent around 200 days abroad on a humanitarian operation .
Law made in 2012 denies migrant visas to those out UK for over 180 days .
Rule to be applied retrospectively so it takes her previous trip into account .
Despite working for a Government-funded group, she must leave Britain .
She believes inflexibility will stop top professionals wanting to work in UK .

summary: Kunming has banned new firewood chicken restaurants to curb air pollution, and existing ones must switch to cleaner fuels like charcoal. The dish, popular in the city, was estimated to burn 550 kg of firewood per 30‑seat restaurant, worsening smog. The move fits China’s wider campaign to reduce coal‑based pollution amid growing public discontent.
reference:
The city of Kunming has stopped granting licenses to new restaurants serving ‘firewood chicken’
The popular dish involves burning lots of wood, releasing harmful gasses .
Officials have instructed existing premises to use different fuel for the dish .
The ban is understood as local government’s attempt to improve air quality .

summary: Mike Tyson warns Mayweather that he must change strategy to beat Pacquiao, citing Pacquiao’s relentless aggression. Mayweather’s odds are strong, but Tyson cites past opponents like Marquez and Bradley as examples of Pacquiao’s weaknesses. Tyson, reflecting on his own career, also highlights financial disparities in boxing while promoting his documentary “Champs” about the sport’s pitfalls.
reference:
Floyd Mayweather and Manny Pacquiao fight on May 2 at the MGM Grand .
Former heavyweight champion Mike Tyson predicts a Pacquiao victory .
Tyson said Filipino's 'hundred punches a round' is too formidable .
He tells Mayweather to come out swinging if he is to be a chance .

summary: Spencer Matthews and other celebrities attend No1 Bootcamp in Ibiza, where they tackle 20‑minute HIIT sessions, three‑hour hikes, boxing, and swimming amid a calorie‑controlled menu. The villa, Casona Morna, offers a scenic setting with massages, group workouts, and a final town night before a weigh‑in. By the end of the week participants lose between four and eleven pounds, with Spencer dropping seven and the biggest loser shedding eleven.
reference:
No1 Bootcamp is tucked into a sprawling farmhouse near Santa Eulalia .
It is a bootcamp to the stars, including Calum Best and Natasha Hamilton .
Classes are run by a former personal training instructor in the RAF .

summary: Jamila Henry, a 21‑year‑old who converted to Islam and allegedly married an ISIS fighter, was arrested at Luton Airport after returning from Syria, while her identical twin Jalila, a self‑proclaimed party girl, expressed shock and disappointment at her sister’s extremist ties. Jalila said her planned girls’ weekend to Amsterdam was ruined by Jamila’s decision to go to Syria, describing her sister’s enthusiasm for the country and the family’s different paths since adolescence. The incident is part of a broader crackdown on British teens suspected of joining ISIS, with passports revoked for several minors and adults involved in facilitating travel to the conflict zone.
reference:
Jamila Henry was arrested at Luton Airport on suspicion of terror offences .
The 21-year-old Muslim convert is thought to have fled jihadis in Syria .
She appeared in court charged with identity document offences today .
Her twin sister Jalila has told of her shock over sibling's link to jihadis .
Claimed the pair grew apart as Jamila became increasingly devout .

summary:
Photographer Pyanek uses a reverse‑lens macro technique to reveal everyday objects in striking, almost deceptive close‑ups.  
The series features 18 images—from a kitchen sponge to a computer keyboard “X” key—each challenging viewers to identify the subject.  
The article invites guesses before revealing the answers in a final list.
reference:
The photographer named Pyanek used a reverse lens macro technique .
His shots are collated in a series called ‘Amazing Worlds Within Our World’
The work features an array of everyday household items, foods and objects .

summary:
Thomas Vermaelen, Barcelona defender, will return next month after a hamstring tear from the 2014 World Cup required surgery.  
Initially, the club opted for non‑surgical treatment, but a specialist later recommended surgery, which Vermaelen is now following.  
He has resumed running and is excited to get back onto the pitch.
reference:
Thomas Vermaelen is on track to return to action in April .
Vermaelen has been out with a hamstring tear that required surgery .
Barcelona defender wrote on Facebook that he's started running again .

summary: A 23‑day‑old infant named Dravyn Johnson, born in Orange County with a half heart that lacked a functional right side, received a lifesaving heart transplant after only two days on the donor list. The transplant, performed at Mattel Children's Hospital, made him the second youngest heart transplant recipient in the U.S., following a 16‑day‑old case from 1994. Dravyn is now healthy, has gone home at five weeks, and has two older brothers.
reference:
Dravyn Johnson spent just two days on the transplant list .
Born with pulmonary atresia meaning only one side of heart formed .
Doctors said he could die 'any day' unless he got donor organ .
He has been allowed home to Orange County at 5-weeks old .

summary:
Gareth Southgate was frustrated by England’s first 25 minutes, even though they beat Germany 3‑2 at the Riverside Stadium.  
The squad’s limited top‑flight experience – 230 appearances among 389 players – underscores concerns that young English talent is under‑used.  
Despite this, the team’s strong performance and key players like James Ward‑Prowse give confidence that England could be serious contenders at the European U21 Championship.
reference:
The Germany Under 21 side beaten by England U21s had 639 top-flight appearances between them: the squad’s combined number was 977 .
Germany  looked a team of stars, passing smoothly in tight areas, winning cute free-kicks and making their experience tell .
It gives credence to the point FA chairman Greg Dyke has made about young English players not getting sufficient opportunities .
When you see the impressive way they tore into Germany, it makes you wonder why some can’t break through the glass ceiling .

summary: Heather Hironimus fled with her 4‑year‑old son to avoid a court‑ordered circumcision, leading a judge to find her in contempt and issue an arrest order. The father, Dennis Nebus, insists the procedure is medically necessary, while Hironimus and her supporters claim the child was terrified of the surgery. Protesters gathered outside the courthouse in Delray Beach to rally in her defense and criticize the judge’s decision.
reference:
Circuit Judge Jeffrey Gillen ordered arrest for mom Heather Hironimus who fled with her son to prevent his circumcision .
Her attorney said his client is staying with  son in a shelter for domestic violence victims because the boy was 'scared to death' of surgery .
Hironimus and the boy's father, Dennis Nebus, were never married but share custody of their child .

summary: McKinzy Livsey, 15, was severely injured when she fell head‑first in a golf cart after swapping seats with friends during a spring break trip in the Arbuckle Mountains. The accident left her with skull fractures, brain swelling, and blood clots, and she was flown to OU Children's Hospital for treatment. Her parents remain horrified but are focusing on recovery and faith as she begins her rehabilitation.
reference:
McKinzy Livsey, 15, has been left with skull fractures, brain swelling, and blood clots after she fell from a golf cart in the Arbuckle Mountains .
McKinzy's father Travis Livsey sad his daughter tried to switch seats with the driver of the golf cart when they hit a bump and she fell out head first .
McKinzy's parents were horrified to receive a call on Sunday with the sounds of their injured daughter screaming in the background .

summary: Teenage rebellion can frighten parents, but Dame Sally Coates argues that a balanced, collaborative approach with schools—rather than confrontation—helps manage misbehaviour. She stresses the importance of open communication, praise over criticism, and avoiding false threats, while also encouraging shared responsibilities at home and in school. Coates has distilled these ideas into her new book, *Headstrong*, offering practical lessons on parenting, discipline, and leadership.
reference:
Dame Sally Coates turned around Burlington Danes School in West London, leading it from failing to an 'outstanding' Ofsted rating .
Superhead says parents who attack their child's school when a teenager misbehaves are on a fast-track to disaster .
Schools should focus more on good manners and presentation in preparing children for the working world .
Mum-of-four says juggling work/life balance comes down to good organisation...and lots of delegation .

summary: St. Paul’s Cathedral hosted a state‑level remembrance of Afghanistan veterans, attended by the Queen, Prince Philip, and senior royals, with 453 Elizabeth Crosses presented to next‑of‑kin of those killed. Families and veterans, though many were ill or missed the service, took part in prayers, speeches and a medal procession. Some political figures departed early, sparking controversy over their attendance.
reference:
Country gathered to honour Afghanistan campaign at St Paul's Cathedral .
Queen led the nation's tribute, supported by her husband, Prince Philip .
All the senior members of the Royal Family and political leaders attended .
Several children were wearing medals of fathers who never returned .

summary: The Productivity Commission proposes a childcare subsidy of $7.20 per hour, with parents paying any excess cost. In Sydney and Melbourne, average daily childcare costs are $138 and $107, far above the benchmark. The new scheme will replace the current childcare rebate and benefit programs.
reference:
Parents in Sydney and Melbourne are worried after out-of-pocket childcare costs may skyrocket if new benchmark figure is adopted .
The Productivity Commission proposed $7.20 per hour as the benchmark .
Parents will have to cover extra cost if childcare is over $79 a day .
Average price for Sydney childcare is $138 per day and $107 in Melbourne .

summary: Deputy U.S. Marshal Josie Wells, 27, was fatally shot during a shootout at Elm Grove Motel in Scotlandville, Louisiana, while pursuing fugitive Jamie D. Croom. Croom, 31, was also shot and taken to a hospital, where his condition has not been released, and he is charged with Wells’ murder. No other officers were injured, and law‑enforcement officials have expressed a somber response to the incident.
reference:
Deputy U.S. Marshal Josie Wells, 27, was killed around 11am on Tuesday at Elm Grove Motel in Scotlandville - an area north of Baton Rouge, LA .
Fugitive, Jamie D. Croom, 31,  was shot  and taken to a hospital where his condition has not been released .
Croom was on the run since February 18 shooting when he was accused of killing Lechelle Rita Williams, 42, and her 38-year-old brother Sinica Lee .

summary: Usain Bolt will return to the United States for the first time in five years, competing at the Adidas Grand Prix Diamond League meeting in New York City on June 13. Organisers have not yet confirmed whether he will run the 100 m or 200 m, but he holds the world records in both events. The 28‑year‑old sprinter is also scheduled to compete in Rio, Paris, and Lausanne as he prepares for the 2015 World Championships in Beijing.
reference:
Usain Bolt broke his first world record in New York, running 9.72 seconds .
2008 was the last time he ran in New York, and 2010 the last time in the US .
He will return for a Diamond League meeting in New York on June 13 .
In a statement, Bolt said he is excited to return to the venue of his success .

summary: Wales coach Warren Gatland has signed four players to national dual contracts, keeping them with their regional clubs while making them available for the national team. The deals include Ospreys’ Jones and Scarlets’ Williams, who were key in recent Six Nations victories. The move is aimed at protecting regional rugby, securing top talent and keeping Wales competitive for the title.
reference:
Wales took their number of players signing National Dual Contracts to 12 .
Alun Wyn Jones, Dan Biggar, Scott Williams and Gareth Anscombe are latest to join the likes Sam Warburton and Rhodri Jones .
Coach Warren Gatland says signings are a 'great benefit' to national side .
Wales face Italy in their final RBS Six Nations fixture on Saturday .

summary: A school bus with nine students veered off the road and crashed into an occupied home in Blue Bell, Philadelphia. No injuries were reported to the students, driver, or residents, and the driver was taken to hospital for evaluation. The house was unharmed after the bus pierced its front window.
reference:
No injuries were reported following the crash on Tuesday at 7.45am, according to Whitpain Township police .
Students ranging from kindergarten to eighth grade from St Helena School were on the bus at the time of crash .
A resident was on the second floor of the home but he was not injured .

summary: A 2008 ordinance banning stand‑alone fast‑food restaurants in South Los Angeles had little effect on the food environment because such outlets were already rare and the ban did not target small stores or strip‑mall restaurants. Despite the ban, obesity rates rose 12 % over three years—reaching 75 % by 2011—while soft‑drink consumption fell citywide, indicating the measure did not curb weight gain. Experts say the law’s symbolic value is limited and that broader strategies, such as improving access to affordable, healthy food, are needed to tackle the region’s obesity crisis.

Study shows law only banned construction and expansion of stand-alone fast-food restaurants, which are rare in the area to begin with .
